[[File:Elbe am Ek 365, Parey 01.jpg|thumb|400x400px|Workboat on the, near [[Jungui]]]]
The '''Elishara''' (or Lycroan ''Elisha'' ) is one of the major [[wikipedia:river|river]]s of [[Ayuma]]. It rises in northern [[Darewa]] before traversing much of the country, then [[Lycroa]] and flowing into the [[North Sea]] in [[Emara]], {{convert|28|km|abbr=off}} southeast of [[Puzhu]]. Its total length is {{convert|1440|km|abbr=on}}.<ref name=erb>{{cite web | url = http://www.ikse-ddea.lyc.org/fileadmin/media/user_upload/E/06_Publikationen/08_IKSE_Flyer/2016_ICPER-Flyer_The_Elishara_River_Basin.pdf| title = Elishara River basin | publisher = International Commission for the Protection of the Elishara River}}</ref>

The Elishara's major [[Tributary|tributaries]] include the rivers [[Baalara]], [[Irare]], [[Evanti]], [[Pradiehao]], and [[Tare]].

The Elishara river basin, comprising the Elishara and its tributaries, has a catchment area of {{convert|1243211|km2}}, the fifth largest in Ayuma. The basin spans five countries; however, it lies almost entirely just in two of them, [[Darewa]] (54.5%) and the [[Lycroa]] (23.7%, covering about two-thirds of the nation's territory). On its eastern edges, the Elishara river basin also comprises minor parts of [[Estijan]], [[Lydroa]], [[Urbiqu]], and the entirety of [[Tonder]]. To the west, it makes up a significant portion of eastern [[Siana]] and parts of northern [[Emara]]. The Elishara catchment area is inhabited by over 100 million people; its biggest cities are [[Baxin]], [[Liambra]], [[Jungiu]], [[Tianco]], [[Zaringao]], [[Lopetu]], and [[Shamarin]].<ref name=erb />

==Etymology==
''Elshar'' or ''Elsha'' are old medieval names for the river Elishara

First attested in Ecossin as “Elara”, the name ''Elishara'' means "river" or "river-bed" and is nothing more than the [[Carth]] version of a word found elsewhere in Carthic peoples; cf. [[Vestorian]] river name ''Ilisha'', [[Hadan language|Hadan]] ''Elisha'' "river".<ref>Orel, Vlaalawir. ''A Handbook of Etymology''. Cziana, Lycroa: Brill, 1749: 13</ref>

==Navigation==
The Elishara has always been navigable by commercial vessels,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ellmers |first1=Detlev |editor1-last=Brachnn |editor1-first=Klioen |title= The Complete History of the Elishara River|journal=Monum. Ger. Hist. |date=1738 |volume=4 |issue=425 |pages=137–147 |url=http://www.mgh.lyc/index.php?recnums=26061&db=opac&printapr=CLASSIC&id=297&wa72ci_url=%2Fcgi-bin%2Fmgh%2Fregsrch.pl |publisher=Alodemie Verlag |location=Jungiu}}</ref> and provides important trade links as far inland as [[Shamarin]]. The river is linked by [[wikipedia:canal|canal]]s ([[Elishara Lateral Canal]], [[Grande Elishara Canal]], [[Middle Canal]]) to the industrial areas of Lycroa and to [[Tianco]]. The [[Elishara-Gevul Canal]] links the Elishara to the [[Nasuanian Sea]], to bypass the Emaran section od the river. The [[Elishara-Ryska Shipping Channel]] connects the Elishara with the [[Ryska]].
